predictions.rationale: Lives in the util.logging package and offers timing/trace facilities that are typically used to emit detailed debug-level performance messages, directly supporting the logging/trace feature.
Also in util.logging; installs a JVM-wide handler that logs uncaught AWT exceptions, providing developers with internal diagnostics – clearly part of the logging/trace infrastructure.
Responsible for reading/writing configuration options; contains code paths to enable/disable or configure logging levels, thus refining the logging feature.
Application entry point; sets up global environment including initialization of logging (e.g., log4j or java.util.logging) based on command-line flags and configuration.
Defines keys and defaults for stored preferences; includes keys for log level and debug settings, thereby directly supporting runtime control of logging.
Specialised exception handler that captures uncaught exceptions and logs them, complementing the debug/trace mechanism.
Presents logged exceptions to the user/developer; tightly coupled with the logging system to display collected trace information.
Developer-oriented module; typically provides tools such as log viewers or toggles for verbose/debug output, thus assisting in focused problem tracing.
Central application API; contains constants and helpers for global facilities like logging, enabling other parts of ArgoUML to emit consistent debug messages.
Core event dispatcher; often instrumented with trace statements to follow internal behaviour, therefore directly contributing to the logging mechanism.
